# Proverbs 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** You can make all the plans you want, but what actually comes out of your mouth is ultimately from the LORD.

**2** People always think they're doing the right thing, but the LORD looks at what's really driving them.

**3** Hand your work over to the LORD, and your plans will actually succeed.

**4** The LORD made everything with a purpose — even the wicked have a role to play when judgment comes.

**5** The LORD can't stand arrogant people. Make no mistake — they will not escape punishment.

**6** Faithful love and honesty make up for wrongdoing, and honoring the LORD is what turns you away from evil.

**7** When the way you live pleases the LORD, He can even make your enemies treat you peaceably.

**8** It's better to have a little and live right than to have massive income gained through injustice.

**9** You can plan your path all you want, but the LORD is the one who directs each step you actually take.

**10** A king's words carry the weight of divine authority; his judgments must not go wrong.

**11** Honest scales and fair weights belong to the LORD — every standard of measurement is His concern.

**12** Kings should despise doing evil, because a throne only stays standing when built on justice.

**13** Kings value people who speak the truth, and they love advisors who say what's right.

**14** A king's anger can mean death, but a wise person knows how to calm it.

**15** When the king smiles on you, it means life. His approval is as refreshing as rain clouds in spring.

**16** Getting wisdom is so much better than getting gold! Choosing understanding beats silver every time.

**17** The road honest people travel avoids evil. Protecting your path is protecting your life.

**18** Pride leads to destruction. Arrogance leads to a fall.

**19** Better to be humble among the lowly than to split stolen goods with the arrogant.

**20** Pay attention to instruction and good things will follow. Trust the LORD, and you'll be truly happy.

**21** A wise person is recognized for their insight, and speaking graciously makes their teaching even more effective.

**22** Good sense is a life-giving spring for whoever has it, but trying to teach fools is a waste of time.

**23** A wise person's heart guides their words, making everything they say more convincing.

**24** Kind words are like honey — sweet to the taste and good for the body.

**25** There's a road that looks right to a person, but it dead-ends in destruction.

**26** A worker's hunger drives them to work — their stomach keeps them going.

**27** A worthless person digs up trouble, and what comes out of their mouth burns like fire.

**28** A troublemaker stirs up conflict, and a gossip can destroy the closest friendship.

**29** A violent person lures their neighbor and leads them down a dangerous road.

**30** When someone squints their eyes and presses their lips together, they've already decided to do wrong.

**31** Gray hair is a beautiful crown — earned by living a righteous life.

**32** Controlling your temper is more impressive than being a war hero, and mastering yourself is greater than conquering a city.

**33** People roll the dice, but every outcome is decided by the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **16:9**: This is one of the most humbling verses in the Bible — you can plan all you want, but God is the one who actually decides where your feet go.

- **16:18**: Probably the most famous proverb ever written. Pride always, always comes before a fall. Not sometimes — always.

- **16:24**: Beautiful and practical — kind words literally heal. They're sweet and nourishing, like honey for the soul and medicine for the body.

— PNEUMA
